title: Wealth advisors monthly
transcript:
Grace Lin: Morning everyone, let's get started. Four items today: Q3 rebalancing cycle, cash management sweep review, KYC refresh changes, and the client review calendar for September. Then action items. Jonathan, can you take notes?
Jonathan Chandler: Sure, I'll capture owners and dates as we go.
Grace Lin: Great. Janet, start us off on rebalancing.
Janet Brown: Thanks. The quarterly rebalance for the low-risk models is staged in PortfolioMgr. Drift is mostly in the fixed income sleeve, which is running about 2.5% over target after the August rally in short-duration paper. Equity is slightly under. I'd like to run the trades the week of September 8 so we're not trading into the month-end noise.
Michael Castillo: Any concern with pricing? Last quarter we had stale marks on a couple of munis that threw off the drift numbers.
Janet Brown: Good point. PricingSvc has been stable since the fix, but I'll pull a stale-price exception report before we release anything. If any bond is more than two days stale, I'll flag it and we hand-price it.
Tricia Kelly: I'd add that we should freeze model changes during the rebalance window. Last time somebody tweaked the allocation mid-run and half the accounts rebalanced to the old targets.
Grace Lin: Agreed. Decision: model freeze from September 4 through September 12. Janet owns the stale price check, Tricia owns communicating the freeze to the advisors.
Tricia Kelly: Will do, I'll post it in #wealth-team today.
Grace Lin: Next, cash management. Kelly, you raised this one.
Kelly Robinson: Yes. We have a few low-risk clients with big idle balances in cash management accounts, and with rates where they are, the sweep yield is lagging what they could get in short Treasuries. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0130}} is a good example. The brokerage account {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00275}} is fully invested, but the linked cash account {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00276}} has been sitting at a high balance for months.
Jonathan Chandler: Is James Anderson the RM on that one? He should be in the loop before anyone reaches out.
Kelly Robinson: Yes, he's the RM. I'll send him the numbers first. I don't want to approach the client directly without him.
Michael Castillo: Same situation with {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0088}}. {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00188}} holds more cash than their policy statement calls for. They've been with us since mid 2024 and the goal was always to deploy gradually. I'd like to propose a laddered Treasury purchase out of {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00187}} funded from the cash side.
Janet Brown: Make sure the investment policy statement supports a ladder out to twelve months. I recall their liquidity needs were conservative.
Michael Castillo: Right, I'll re-read the IPS and confirm with the client on the next call. I'll check the contact details in ClientHub rather than relying on my notes.
Grace Lin: Decision: no changes to either account until the RM has spoken with the client and the IPS is confirmed. Kelly, put together a one-page summary of idle cash across the low-risk book, no client identifiers in the deck, just counts and balance bands. Due September 11.
Kelly Robinson: Got it.
Grace Lin: Third item, KYC. Jonathan, you've been following the ownership change.
Jonathan Chandler: Yes. KYCPipeline moves from Operations to Compliance on October 6. For us, the practical impact is the periodic refresh requests. Right now we chase Operations when a document is stuck. After the sixth, it goes to Compliance, and the queue may be prioritized differently.
Tricia Kelly: Do we know if the refresh cadence is changing for low-risk clients?
Jonathan Chandler: Not yet. Marcus Bell's team said they'd publish the updated procedure before the cutover. I'll ask for a draft so we can review it before it lands.
Michael Castillo: Also worth knowing that refreshed documents land in DocVault, and the pipeline pulls client records from ClientHub. If our CRM data is stale, the refresh bounces. We should clean up addresses and employment fields beforehand.
Kelly Robinson: I can take a pass on my own book. I have maybe fifteen records that look old.
Grace Lin: Good. Let's make it everyone's book. Each advisor audits their ClientHub records for KYC-relevant fields by September 25. Jonathan, you request the draft procedure from Compliance and circulate it by September 18.
Jonathan Chandler: Noted.
Grace Lin: Last item, client review calendar. We have about thirty annual reviews due in September and October. Janet, how are the portfolio managers on capacity?
Janet Brown: Fine if we batch them. I'd rather do reviews in the second half of September, after the rebalance, so the numbers we show are post-trade.
Tricia Kelly: That makes sense. I'd rather not present a portfolio we're about to change.
Grace Lin: Decision: reviews are scheduled after September 15. Advisors send invites by September 10. Wealth associates will prep the materials, and please remember not to email statements outside the secure portal.
Michael Castillo: One more thing. For {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0088}}, they asked for a callback about the ladder. I'll use the number on file in ClientHub, {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0088}}, and confirm by email at {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0088}} only for scheduling, nothing with balances.
Grace Lin: Good practice. Let's recap actions. Janet: stale-price report before the September 8 rebalance. Tricia: freeze announcement today. Kelly: idle cash summary by September 11, and numbers to James Anderson on {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0130}}. Michael: IPS check and ladder proposal. Jonathan: Compliance draft procedure by September 18. Everyone: ClientHub audit by September 25 and review invites by September 10.
Jonathan Chandler: I'll send these out in the follow-up note this afternoon.
Grace Lin: Thanks all. Next meeting is September 25. Have a good weekend.
